whatItIs.text: A firm cow's-milk cheese aged 3-24 months, born in the Somerset village of Cheddar and now made worldwide — 'cheddar' names a style, not a protected place.

historyNote.text: Cheddar Gorge's caves gave the original wheels their steady humidity; the 19th-century dairyman Joseph Harding, 'the father of cheddar', standardised the method and spread it worldwide. In the Second World War nearly all British milk went into one 'government cheddar', wiping out most of the country's other cheeses — over 3,500 producers before the First World War, fewer than 100 after the second.

howToChoose.text: Milder and cheaper suits cooking, aged cloth-bound suits eating; avoid oily, sweaty packaging and check that 'red cheddar' isn't just colouring.

storage.text: Wrap in waxed or cheese paper and keep in the fridge's warmest spot. The rulebook has the windows and mould guidance.
storage.note: hard-cheese storage and mould guidance live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Hard cheese ends melt into sauce, rarebit, or nachos; the rind-less trimmings of aged cheddar grate and freeze well for last-minute toasties.

substitutions.note: melts smoother, milder; no aged sharpness
sweeter and crumblier; sometimes sold as 'red cheddar'
